channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Trump Says He and Xi Talked Extensively About Taiwan
item.description: President Trump stated he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed Taiwan extensively during his visit to Beijing. The two leaders emphasized stability upon Trump's departure. No significant agreements were reached on Taiwan, the war in Iran, or other contentious issues. As President Trump left Beijing, he and Xi Jinping, China’s leader, played up stability.

item.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
item.description: Mali's armed forces, aided by Russian mercenaries, conducted airstrikes against a coalition of Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists. This offensive follows an advance by the rebel alliance. The junta is working to retain control amid the ongoing conflict in the west African nation.

item.title: Pakistan faces pressure over mediator role in Iran war
item.description: Pakistan is mediating between Iran and Israel. This role places Islamabad in a difficult position. It must balance relations with the United States, Iran, China, and Gulf states. A recent US media report has increased scrutiny on Pakistan's involvement. With Pakistan stepping in the middle of a major geopolitical conflict, Islamabad is forced to balance between Washington, Tehran, Beijing and key Gulf allies.

item.title: How Starmer survives as Farage waits in wings
item.description: United Kingdom politics faces instability with high-profile resignations and a High profile resignations, a prime minister on the edge and populists on the up. UK politics is far from dull. DW explains what's going on in Keir Starmer's Labour party and with Nigel Farage.

item.title: 'Everything was in greyscale': What it is like to survive a suicide attempt and recover
item.description: Recovering from a suicide attempt is a complex process. The path of recovering after once thinking of ending one's life is rarely straightforward. But for those who have lived through such a crisis, and the caregivers who walked beside them, they hope no one has to face it alone.

item.title: US-China summit exposes Trump's limits on Iran war, Taiwan
item.description: Donald Trump concluded a two-day visit to Beijing. Donald Trump hopes to have China help him end the war in Iran, but this goal seemed far from guaranteed as he wrapped up his two-day visit to Beijing. Xi Jinping, in turn, took the chance to warn the US over Taiwan.

item.description: Donald Trump stated the US and China share similar views on ending the war in China calls for ceasefire and opening of seaway, while Donald Trump says Xi feels ‘very similar’ about ending the war in IranTrump in China – latest updatesDonald Trump has claimed that the US and China “feel very similar” about ending the war in Iran but offered no details about a possible breakthrough. The US president was speaking alongside Xi Jinping of China at the Zhongnanhai garden in Beijin.

item.title: Trump and Xi’s suits put ‘chameleon effect’ to test in Beijing
item.description: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping wore strikingly similar blue suits during their Mirroring of each other’s attire may signal alignment – though the look wasn’t a huge departure for either leaderWhen Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met for a welcome ceremony in Tiananmen Square this week with the world’s gaze on them, they mirrored one another in strikingly similar suits. Both were blue, single-breasted with flap pockets.

item.title: Somalia at ‘real risk of famine’ as Middle East war fallout continues
item.description: UN aid teams warned Somalia faces a real risk of famine. At least six million people in Somalia are going days without enough food, UN aid teams warned on Friday, highlighting that nearly two million of this number are young children “at high risk of illness or death”.

item.title: CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims
item.description: CIA Director John Ratcliffe met Cuban officials in Havana. The Cuban government stated the meeting aimed to improve dialogue. This occurred amid complex bilateral relations between the two countries. CIA director has met officials in Havana for talks, Cuba claims.

item.title: Newsom condemns GOP redistricting efforts; Louisiana approves plan to erase majority-Black district
item.description: U. S. President Trump arrived in Beijing for high-stakes talks with Xi Jinping. Security is heightened as trade, AI, and the war in Iran are set to dominate the summit. The leaders aim to improve the bilateral relationship.

item.title: HIV prevention and treatment services faltering, warns UNAIDS
item.description: UNAIDS warned that HIV prevention and treatment services are faltering. Decades of gains in the fight against AIDS are under growing threat as donor funding declines and community-based health services collapse in some of the world’s most vulnerable countries, the head of the joint UN programme on HIV/AIDS warned on Thursday.

item.title: Malnutrition in Somalia, hunger crisis in DR Congo, energy shortages in Cuba
item.description: UN-backed food security experts warned nearly six million people in Nearly six million people in Somalia – almost a third of the population analysed – are projected to face acute hunger between April and June, with 1.9 million expected to experience emergency levels, UN-backed food security experts warned on Thursday.

item.title: UN welcomes $1.8 billion US boost for humanitarian operations
item.description: The United States announced $1.8 billion in new humanitarian funding. This boost will support United Nations and partner aid operations globally. The funding arrives as rising needs and shortfalls force agencies to reduce assistance. An additional $1.8 billion in US humanitarian funding will allow the United Nations and its partners to expand emergency relief operations reaching millions of people worldwide, as rising global needs and funding shortfalls force aid agencies to scale back assistance.

item.title: Yemen parties agree under UN mediation to release 1,600 detainees
item.description: Yemen's warring parties agreed to release over 1,600 detainees. The deal was brokered by the United Nations in Jordan. This marks the largest prisoner exchange since the civil war began. The agreement offers a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts. More than 1,600 conflict-related detainees in Yemen will be released under a UN-brokered agreement reached after months of negotiations in Jordan, marking the largest prisoner release deal since the country’s civil war began and offering a rare sign of progress in stalled peace efforts.

item.title: UN pleads for Equatorial Guinea not to send US asylum seekers to their home countries: ‘Their life
item.description: United Nations human rights experts publicly urged Equatorial Guinea to stop returning US deportees. The experts cited reports of political violence, torture, and death faced by individuals sent back to their home countries. Deportees described being held in prison-like conditions.
